findings.message: This change makes `--_fs-base` untyped by switching its syntax from `<length>` to `*`. `--_fs-base` drives every `--fs-*` token in the design system, so this global change is out of scope for a Legend feature, and nothing in the diff needs it. With `*`, an invalid value such as `--_fs-base: large` is no longer rejected at parse time and does not fall back to the 1rem initial value. Instead, every `calc()` built from `--fs-*` becomes invalid, and font sizes break silently across all components. The property also stops being animatable or interpolable. Please revert it, or justify it and test it separately.

This is a breaking change for anyone using `Legend` directly. (1) `className` used to be applied to the `role="list"` flex row and now goes on a new outer wrapper, so consumer styles aimed at the list (for example `flex-wrap` or `justify-content`) stop working. (2) The default `justify-content: center` was removed and the root is now an `inline-flex` aligned to flex-start. Every standalone legend that used to be centered is now left-aligned unless the caller adds `alignSelf="center"`, which the PR only did for the built-in charts. The PR has no changeset or migration note even though it changes behavior visibly.

The visible label and the list's accessible name are the same string, so the visible label is applied as a duplicated `aria-label` and not linked with `aria-labelledby`. Screen readers read the heading text and then announce "list, Sales by product" again. It also breaks the link between the visible label and the name, which matters for translation and voice-control. Give the label an id (`useId`) and point to it with `aria-labelledby`. Separately, `label=""` hides the visible label (falsy check) but sets `aria-label=""` (`??` only checks for null or undefined), which leaves the list with no accessible name instead of falling back to "Chart legend".

Size variants use `[data-size]` attribute selectors. The package conventions (AGENTS.md) say: "Variants and sizes: use cva-generated classes, not data-attributes; data-attribute selectors for RAC state only." Generate a size class with `cva` instead. Also, `.root` sets `font-size: var(--fs-sm)` and the `md` variant sets the same value again, which is redundant.
`font-weight: bold` breaks the package rule: "Font-weight: use `bolder` when text needs bold... No numeric weights or `bold`." Use `bolder`.

The `useMemo` here adds complexity without measurable benefit. The `series` arrays in the examples, and likely in most callers, are new on every render, so the memo is recomputed every time anyway. Mapping a handful of items is cheap. Render the items inline.

These tests don't check the behavior they describe. `assume(locator).exists()` only checks that a Locator object exists, and Locators are always truthy whether or not anything matches, so the label test passes even if no list has the accessible name. The 'stacks items vertically' test only counts list items and never checks the vertical layout (for example, `flex-direction: column` or the items' y-positions). Use `await expect.element(...).toBeInTheDocument()` and assert on the layout.

The horizontal list doesn't wrap (no `flexWrap`), and the root is now an `inline-flex` box centered with `alignSelf`. In both charts the legend's parent has `overflow: hidden`, so if a chart has many series or long names, items that overflow the chart width are clipped. Readers lose series names with no visual sign that anything is missing. Since the PR's goal is to handle tight horizontal space, add `flexWrap="wrap"` for horizontal orientation.

Breaking visual change to the public `Legend` component. The root used to be a block-level flex row with `justify-content: center`. It is now `display: inline-flex` with `align-items: flex-start`, so any consumer that renders `<Legend>` on its own (outside BarChart/LineChart) will see the legend jump from centered to start-aligned. Only the built-in charts were patched with `alignSelf="center"`. Either keep centering as the default (for example, center the list inside a full-width root) or document this as a breaking change in the changeset/release notes.

This changes the global `@property --_fs-base` syntax from `<length>` to `*`. That is unrelated to the legend and affects every `--fs-*` token in the design system. It removes type validation, so invalid values are no longer rejected and replaced by the 1rem initial value. It also stops the value from being computed to an absolute length, so relative units now resolve wherever the token is used, and the property can no longer be interpolated or animated. The legend doesn't need this change. Nothing in the PR justifies it beyond 'broader compatibility', so it should be reverted or moved to its own reviewed change.

The visible label and the list's name are wired together by duplicating the string into `aria-label`, not by referencing the label element. The text isn't programmatically linked, and some screen readers will announce it twice (once as text, once as the list name). Give the label an id (`useId`) and use `aria-labelledby` on the list. Also, `label ?? 'Chart legend'` lets `label=""` produce an empty `aria-label`, which leaves the list unnamed. Use `label || 'Chart legend'` or check the trimmed value.

Size variants use `[data-size]` attribute selectors. The package conventions (AGENTS.md) say variants and sizes must use cva-generated classes, and that data-attribute selectors are reserved for RAC state. The `.root` base rule and the `[data-size="md"]` rule are also redundant, since both set `font-size: var(--fs-sm)`.
`font-weight: bold` breaks the documented project rule (variables.css and AGENTS.md): use `bolder` when text needs bold, and don't use `bold` or numeric weights.

The `useMemo` keyed on `series` adds overhead without benefit. Callers almost always pass a new array literal on each render (as every example does), so the memo never hits. Map the items inline as before.

`LegendProps` now spreads every remaining `FlexProps`, including `role`, `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`, onto the outer wrapper and not onto the `role="list"` element. A consumer who passes `aria-label` to name the legend will label a generic div, while the list still announces as 'Chart legend'. Either omit these ARIA props or forward them to the list.

The new browser tests don't really check anything. `getByRole`/`getByText` return locator objects, so `assume(locator).exists()` passes even when nothing matches. They should use `await expect.element(...).toBeInTheDocument()` or similar. The 'stacks items vertically' test only counts list items and never checks the vertical layout (for example, `flex-direction: column` or item positions), so it would also pass for a horizontal legend.
